figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Overview and initial biochemical analysis of SmaO and
SmaX. (A) Biosynthetic gene cluster containing SmaA, SmaO, and
SmaX. (B) Amino acid sequence of precursor SmaA. The double
glycine motif is colored in blue and the aspartates modified by SmaO
and SmaX are colored in red. The LahT150 cleavage site separates the
leader and core peptide. (C) Mass analysis of SmaA or its modified
variants coexpressed with or without SmaO or SmaX. Full length and
the LahT150-cleaved peptides were analyzed by MALDI-TOF-MS
(left) and H-ESI-HRMS (right), respectively. Calculated and
observed mass values can be found in Supplementary Data set.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. SmaO is an Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent aspartate hydroxylase. (A) H-ESI-MS/MS analysis of LahT150 cleaved SmaA(O).
Fragments observed with the addition of two oxygens (+32 Da) are annotated in blue, one oxygen (+16 Da) in red, and none in black. All the mass
values with the exception of b20 support hydroxylation in Asp31 and Asp33. (B) In vitro reactions of SmaO. The reaction mixture was incubated
for 1 h with each 2-oxoglutarate and Fe(II) added (+) or not added (−). (C) Structure and key 2D NMR correlations of SmaA30−38(O) (1). The
chemical shift values of the α- and β-carbons and protons of Hya are shown in red. (D) Mass analysis of the SmaA variants coexpressed with SmaO.
The modified sequence of each precursor is annotated in red. X-axes are shifted to align the peaks. Calculated and observed mass values can be
found in Supplementary Data set.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. SmaX produces aminomalonic acid by cleaving C−C bond in β-hydroxyaspartic acid. (A) Reaction scheme of the SmaO−SmaX cascade,
compared with that of PhnY−PhnZ. SmaO and PhnY introduce a hydroxyl group (blue) followed by the oxidative C−C or C−P bond cleavage
(red) by SmaX and PhnZ, respectively. Relative mass values to Asp (M) are M + 16 for SmaO and M-14 for SmaX. The SmaX product Ama is
further decarboxylated in MALDI-TOF-MS to yield glycine with a mass value of M-58. (B) Mass analysis of the in vitro SmaX reaction with various
metal ion cofactors. The substrate peptide SmaA28−57(O) (40 μM), SmaX (1 μM) and 10 μM of each metal were mixed with 1 mM DTT and
incubated at 25 °C for 1 h, followed by MALDI-TOF-MS analysis. (C) H-ESI-MS/MS analysis of LahT150-cleaved SmaA(OX). Fragments
observed with two decarboxylated residues (−88 Da) are annotated in blue, one decarboxylated residue (−44 Da) in red, and no decarboxylated
residues in black. All the mass values with the exception of b26 support decarboxylation in Ama31 and Ama33. Calculated and observed mass
values can be found in Supplementary Data set. (D) Structure and key 2D NMR correlations of SmaA30−38(OX) (2). The chemical shift values of
α-carbons and protons of Ama are shown in red.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. SmaX is a unique HD domain enzyme. (A) Superposition of the crystal structure of PhnZ (PDB 4MLN;44 Blue) and AlphaFold3-
predicted structure of SmaX with Fe3+ (Pink). (B) Fe-binding site of PhnZ. Metal binding residues are colored in dark blue and the substrate mimic
of PhnZ (ODV, ([(1R)-2-amino-1-hydroxyethyl] phosphonic acid) is colored in orange. (C) Predicted Fe-binding site of SmaX with SmaA(O).
The three residues located within 4 Å of Fe in the predicted structure are colored in magenta and the hydroxyaspartate residue of SmaA(O) is
colored in yellow. The ipTM score between SmaX and SmaA is 0.78. The pLDDT scores of H39, H63, and N143 are 95, 97, and 96, respectively.29

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Representative biosynthetic gene clusters containing Fe(II)/2OG−SmaX homologue pairs. They are expected to produce graspetide (A),
lanthipeptide (B), triceptide (C), linear azol(in)e-containing peptide (D), thioamitide (E), or uncharacterized class of RiPPs or nonribosomal
peptides (G). Domains annotated with three letter amino acid abbreviation is the adenylation domain installing the corresponding amino acid. The
number of BGCs in each category is shown in bold. SmaX homologues are colored in red, Fe(II)/2OG hydroxylases in blue, putative precursors in
green and putative class defining enzymes in orange. Putative cross-links are shown as dotted lines.
